title: The Spirit and Mortification of Sin
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
searchTerms: The Spirit and Mortification of Sin
definition: The Spirit and mortification of sin teaches that believers put sin to death by the power of the Holy Spirit. Sin must not be excused, hidden, managed, or obeyed; it must be fought through Spirit-empowered repentance and faith.
summary: The Spirit and mortification of sin teaches that believers put sin to death by the power of the Holy Spirit. Sin must not be excused, hidden, managed, or obeyed; it must be fought through Spirit-empowered repentance and faith.
christFocus: Christ died and rose to break sin’s mastery, and the Spirit applies that victory in believers. By the Spirit, God’s people put to death the deeds of the body and live in the freedom of Christ.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Believers are not called to make peace with sin. Scripture commands them to put to death what is earthly, crucify the flesh with its passions and desires, and live according to the Spirit.

Mortification is not self-hatred or despair. It is the Spirit-empowered rejection of sin because believers belong to Christ. Sin is no longer their master, and they are called to fight from the freedom Christ gives.

The Spirit exposes sin, strengthens repentance, renews desires, and gives power for obedience. Believers must act, but they do not act alone. They put sin to death by the Spirit.

This work is ongoing. Old patterns may resist, but the Spirit patiently trains God’s people to say no to ungodliness and live for Christ.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people try to manage sin instead of killing it. Others grow discouraged because willpower fails. This doctrine teaches that sin is serious, but the Spirit’s power is real.

It is especially important for recovery, temptation, and hidden struggles. Christ does not call His people to pretend; He calls them to bring sin into the light and fight by the Spirit’s grace.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Name sin honestly and bring it before God. Do not excuse it as personality, pain, habit, or weakness only. Depend on the Spirit, use Scripture, confess where needed, flee temptation, and practice obedience. Fight sin as someone who belongs to Christ and has the Spirit’s help.
